incoming.name: Sumer

outgoing.name: Ancient Greece
outgoing.excerpt: In ancient Greece this led to confusion whether to eat the plant at the beginning or the end of a meal.

outgoing.name: Ancient Rome
outgoing.excerpt: The Romans took advantage of this property by eating lettuce at the end of a meal to induce sleep.

outgoing.name: Asia
outgoing.excerpt: The wild predecessor of our modern lettuce, Lactuca serriola, can still be seen all over Europe and the more temperate parts of Asia.

outgoing.name: China
outgoing.excerpt: In some places, including China, lettuce is typically eaten cooked and use of the stem are as important as use of the leaf.
